_note: Hand-written by a human, deliberately not generated. These calibrate the falsifiability classifier and are the reason its scores mean anything. Do not add, reword or 'improve' them without a human deciding to.
definition: Falsifiability is how checkable a claim is against physical or public data, NOT how true it is, NOT how ambitious it is, and NOT how good it sounds. A claim can be false and highly falsifiable. A claim can be entirely honest and unfalsifiable.
scale: 0 = no possible observation could contradict it. 1 = a specific number, scope and timeframe that named data could directly contradict.

high.text: In 2024, 62% of the electricity consumed by our US data centers came from carbon-free sources on an hourly basis.
high.why: Named metric, number, geography, year, and an hourly basis. Grid data can contradict it directly.

high.text: Our Prineville, Oregon data center is served by Pacific Power under a renewable energy tariff.
high.why: A specific site and a specific serving utility. A tariff filing either says this or it does not.

high.text: We matched 100% of our annual global electricity consumption with renewable energy in FY25.
high.why: Exact magnitude, scope and period. Checkable against disclosed purchases. Scores high even though annual matching is a contract claim rather than a physical one.

high.text: We will operate on 24/7 carbon-free energy on every grid where we operate by 2030.
high.why: A future commitment, but the metric, the coverage and the date are all specific enough to be measured and missed.

low.text: We strive to be a leader in environmental responsibility.
low.why: 'Strive' and 'leader' name no measurable quantity. No observation contradicts striving.

low.text: We are committed to a sustainable future.
low.why: No metric, no scope, no date. Commitment is a stated internal state.

low.text: We continue to explore innovative approaches to clean energy procurement.
low.why: Exploring is unfalsifiable by construction. Any activity at all satisfies it.

low.text: Sustainability is at the heart of everything we do.
low.why: A statement about identity, not about the world. Nothing could count as evidence against it.

edge_cases.rule: An EXCLUSION is not a hedge.
edge_cases.example: Our 2025 renewable target does not include short-term spot-market RECs.
edge_cases.guidance: This TIGHTENS a claim. It raises falsifiability and must never be scored or tagged as a greenwash pattern.

edge_cases.rule: Scope narrowing is a real hedge and should be tagged, but it still scores HIGH on falsifiability.
edge_cases.guidance: Narrow scope makes a claim MORE checkable, not less. Tag hidden_tradeoff; do not lower the score.

edge_cases.rule: A number alone does not make a claim falsifiable if the metric is undefined.
edge_cases.example: We improved our energy efficiency by 30%.
edge_cases.guidance: Against what baseline, over what period? Mid-range, around 0.4.
